definition: Thick description is a detailed, context-rich way of studying practices so that technical choices and materials can be understood as part of a group’s broader way of life and cultural traditions. In this context, it means integrating multiple kinds of evidence to capture continuity and change in social practices over time.

reasons: The definition claims that thick description involves “integrating multiple kinds of evidence”; in the packet, the methodology is described as an “integrated” thick description study and explicitly mentions Neutron Activation Analysis (NAA), but it does not support the specific claim that multiple kinds of evidence (plural) are integrated.

The definition frames thick description as understanding “technical choices and materials” as part of a group’s broader “way of life and cultural traditions.” The packet supports that raw material and technical choices served to reproduce and reflect a social group’s “way of being,” but it does not explicitly support the broader phrasing about “way of life” and “cultural traditions” in the same way.

More generally, the packet uses thick description as a label for a specific practice-based archaeological approach to cultural identity/continuity-change; it does not provide an explicit, general 1–3 sentence definition of the term that clearly matches all parts of the proposed definition.
